## Tours including a half-day São Paulo sightseeing excursion

[São Paulo](/brazil/place/sao-paulo/) is often the last major city on a journey through Brazil. Here, travelers can finish their trip with an introduction to local culture and urban life after the natural attractions of Rio de Janeiro and Iguaçu.

Ada Tours offers a specific [half-day São Paulo sightseeing excursion with an English-speaking guide](/brazil/sao-paulo/sao-paulo-city-half-day-english/). It is included in the [9-day group tour "Rio de Janeiro, Iguaçu and São Paulo"](/brazil/tour/rio-iguazu-sao-paulo-group-9-days/). Admission tickets to the attractions visited during the city excursion are also included. The precise order of all stops is not fixed, however, so a visit to a particular museum should not be promised just because it is in the city center.

## How the 9-day journey is organized

The tour connects 3 major destinations within Brazil. Travelers start in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), exploring Sugarloaf Mountain, Corcovado, Santa Teresa and the natural landscapes of Tijuca National Park. The itinerary then moves to the Brazilian side of the waterfalls in [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), including the Macuco Safari boat excursion.

The final stage takes place in São Paulo. A half-day sightseeing excursion is scheduled for day 8, with a hotel-to-airport transfer for departure on day 9. This matters for group planning: sightseeing is already included on the eighth day, while the final day is devoted to departure rather than another full program.

The trip alternates between a major coastal city, national parks and a metropolis with a very different character. São Paulo provides a finale in which natural experiences give way to culture and architecture.

## What you might see in São Paulo and what the excursion actually promises

São Paulo offers many options for city sightseeing. The historic center has squares, cathedrals and municipal buildings; Liberdade introduces Japanese-Brazilian culture; Avenida Paulista is known for modern business districts and cultural institutions.

São Paulo's municipal tourism authority develops separate routes through Liberdade, the historic center and Avenida Paulista. This confirms the appeal of these districts, but **the standalone Ada Tours excursion is described more broadly: a city and cultural overview without a fixed list of individual attractions**. Agree the exact stops with the organizer according to the available time and logistics.

If you want to explore particular museums in depth or devote time to Ibirapuera Park or street art, compare the [historic and modern São Paulo excursion](/brazil/sao-paulo/sao-paulo-historic-modern-graffiti/), which covers different named areas. The [six-hour city tour](/brazil/sao-paulo/sao-paulo-city-tour-6-hours/) also specifically lists many historic-center landmarks.

## Who is the group itinerary designed for?

The confirmed "Rio–Iguaçu–São Paulo" program is designed for a group of **40 participants plus 1 complimentary place (40+1 FOC)**. This is the commercial basis of that particular group offer, not a general Ada Tours rule for every trip.

The itinerary includes English-speaking guides, selected lunches and themed dinners. Domestic and international flights are charged separately. The accommodation terms indicate that the contents of the hotel package need to be confirmed: do not automatically assume every hotel is included without an agreed offer.

This format is useful for corporate travel planners and tourist groups who want to combine three contrasting sides of Brazil. It differs from a private São Paulo city excursion in logistical scope, number of participants and the inclusion of other cities.

## Half a day or a full day in São Paulo?

| Option | Main focus |
|---|---|
| [Half-day excursion](/brazil/sao-paulo/sao-paulo-city-half-day-english/) | General overview before the tour ends |
| [Six-hour excursion](/brazil/sao-paulo/sao-paulo-city-tour-6-hours/) | Landmarks in the old city center |

Do not choose solely by nominal duration. São Paulo is enormous, traffic affects transfers, and time spent in museums and squares depends on the group. A half-day tour gives a general impression of the city but cannot replace exploring all its districts in depth.

For a group trip, identify your essential priorities in advance so the city overview does not turn into an endless succession of transfers. The excursion contents can be agreed within the existing offer.

## Practical details: tickets, language and flights

The half-day excursion includes **an English-speaking guide and admission tickets**. The exact museums and individual ticket prices are not listed, so it would be wrong to assume that entry to any attraction you choose is covered.

The itinerary ends with a departure flight the following day. When booking the entire group tour, compare the schedules of flights between Rio, Iguaçu and São Paulo, baggage allowances, accommodation category and meal inclusions. The standalone excursion and the multi-day itinerary have their own terms.

Other options appear in the [Brazil tour catalog](/brazil/tour/) and the [culture and history section](/interests/culture-and-history/). When choosing, clarify exactly what your selected program includes rather than applying conditions from a neighboring excursion.

## Frequently asked questions about the tour with a half-day São Paulo excursion

### On which day do you visit São Paulo?

On the [9-day group tour](/brazil/tour/rio-iguazu-sao-paulo-group-9-days/), the city sightseeing excursion is on day 8. The airport transfer is scheduled for day 9.

### Is there an English-speaking guide, and are tickets included?

Yes. The [half-day excursion](/brazil/sao-paulo/sao-paulo-city-half-day-english/) explicitly includes an English-speaking guide and admission tickets. The precise ticket list depends on the agreed stops.

### Can the excursion be booked without the full nine-day itinerary?

It has its own [excursion page](/brazil/sao-paulo/sao-paulo-city-half-day-english/). If your accommodation and flights are already arranged, you can discuss booking just the city excursion, subject to its confirmed services.

### Are flights included in the tour price?

Under the terms of the [nine-day itinerary](/brazil/tour/rio-iguazu-sao-paulo-group-9-days/), domestic and international airfare is paid separately. Include these costs in your overall budget independently of the São Paulo excursion.

## São Paulo in 6 hours: historic neighborhoods and main squares

[São Paulo](/brazil/place/sao-paulo/) can easily seem like a city of skyscrapers, business districts and expressways. Yet its history is particularly visible in the old center, where the city's founding site, religious buildings, theaters and historic commercial streets stand close together. **Ada Tours' 6-hour sightseeing excursion** connects these landmarks.

Our route introduces Praça da Sé and the cathedral, Liberdade, the site where São Paulo was founded, Viaduto do Chá, the Municipal Theatre, the square near the railway station, the suburban train station, the Municipal Market, Praça da República and the Terraço Itália building. It is a comprehensive overview of central districts, especially useful for a first visit when you want to understand São Paulo's layout and past before choosing individual museums.

## Praça da Sé and the city's early history

**Praça da Sé** is one of historic São Paulo's main public squares. The cathedral here is notable for its monumental neo-Gothic architecture. Metro lines, pedestrian routes and streams of residents meet around the square, making it a good place to understand how the historic center functions today.

Nearby is **the site of the city's founding**, associated with Jesuit activity in the 16th century. To understand this history, it helps to compare the religious monuments with the transformed urban landscape: old buildings are now surrounded by the streets and infrastructure of a vast metropolis.

The excursion introduces these landmarks. It **does not confirm** that entering the cathedral, visiting exhibitions or taking a specific tour of museum interiors is mandatory. If interior visits interest you, allow for them separately when planning.

## Liberdade: migration history and urban culture

**Liberdade** is known for its strong Japanese and East Asian cultural heritage. Alongside the history of Brazil's urban communities, restaurants, specialist shops, signs and street decorations are prominent here. This stop reveals São Paulo's cultural diversity without traveling far from the central districts.

If your aim is to delve into Japanese migration, try particular dishes or visit a specific museum, allocate extra time. On the six-hour itinerary, Liberdade is one stop within a wider city overview, not a separate food tour.

São Paulo's tourism authorities identify Liberdade and Praça da Sé as significant areas along the central sightseeing route. Opening hours of individual attractions and market spaces still need to be checked for your chosen date.

## Viaduto do Chá, the theater and Praça da República

**Viaduto do Chá**, the Tea Viaduct, connects sections of the historic center. The **Municipal Theatre of São Paulo** stands nearby. Their architecture reflects the period when the city grew rapidly through trade, industry and the arrival of new residents.

The itinerary also includes **Praça da República**, a square by the station and the suburban railway station. These are good places to observe the city's everyday transport and commercial activity. The **Terraço Itália building** is also on the list, as an example of São Paulo's high-rise architecture.

Together, these landmarks tell a connected story of the city center rather than providing unrelated photo stops. However, interior tours, trips up to viewpoints and paid admission require separate confirmation.

## The Municipal Market and everyday city life

**Mercado Municipal** is a famous city market where produce stalls sit alongside places to eat. It offers a different picture of São Paulo after its formal squares and theatrical façades. The excursion visits the market area, but a particular tasting, purchase of food or meal is not automatically included.

If you would like to spend longer here, discuss the balance between historic stops and the market visit. Six hours can fill quickly if a group takes long breaks, enters buildings or encounters heavy traffic.

## How the six-hour tour differs from the extended excursion

The emphasis here is on **the historic center, Liberdade and city monuments**. Do not confuse it with the separate [historic and modern São Paulo excursion](/brazil/sao-paulo/sao-paulo-historic-modern-graffiti/), which also names Avenida Paulista, Ibirapuera Park and a graffiti district. Those places are not automatically included in this six-hour overview.

The choice is straightforward: the six-hour route suits a first encounter with old São Paulo's streets. If you also want to experience contemporary urban culture and street art, compare the programs and realistic transfer times. More options are available in the [São Paulo excursions catalog](/brazil/sao-paulo/). For wider travel, explore [cultural and historical itineraries](/interests/culture-and-history/) and [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/).

## Planning your day

Given the size of the city and heavy traffic, agree in advance on meeting and ending points, the order of stops and how much walking is involved. If parts of the historic center are closed for roadworks or events, the sequence may need adjusting.

Closed shoes are comfortable for exploring the center. Bring drinking water and a small umbrella or light rain protection. Admission fees, guiding language, transportation and group format are agreed before traveling; these services cannot be assumed merely from the "6 hours" title.

## Frequently asked questions about the six-hour São Paulo excursion

### Which places are explicitly listed in the itinerary?

Praça da Sé, the cathedral, Liberdade, São Paulo's founding site, Viaduto do Chá, the Municipal Theatre, the station square, the station, the Municipal Market, Praça da República and Terraço Itália. The order and duration of stops are agreed separately.

### Is Ibirapuera Park included?

The park is not among the stops listed for the six-hour route. It is included in a different sightseeing excursion, so compare the specific itineraries.

### Can you go inside the Municipal Theatre?

The theater building is on the route, but an interior visit and theater tickets have not been separately confirmed. Check access and allow sufficient time in advance if you want this visit.

### Is it a walking tour or a tour with transportation?

The means of traveling between stops are decided when arranging the excursion. Confirm transportation, walking distances and the meeting point before booking.

## Tours with a six-hour São Paulo sightseeing excursion

The [six-hour São Paulo city tour](/brazil/sao-paulo/sao-paulo-city-tour-6-hours/) primarily explores the historic side of the metropolis: Praça da Sé, the cathedral, the Japanese neighborhood of Liberdade, the Municipal Theatre, the market and Praça da República. It is a good introduction for travelers who want to get a feel for the city before heading to other regions.

At Ada Tours, this excursion is connected with the [ten-day Brazil motorcycle tour](/brazil/tour/brazil-motorcycle-tour-10-days/), but its status is important: on day 1 it is **offered as an optional activity if time and interest allow**. Being listed separately in the itinerary does not mean that every participant will automatically take the full city tour or that its cost is covered by the base motorcycle-trip price.

## What is covered in the six-hour city route?

The historic section includes several recognizable stops.

**Praça da Sé and the cathedral** introduce the old center. Here you can see one of the city's major squares and the cathedral's architecture.

**Liberdade** reveals Japanese-Brazilian culture in the urban environment. Its shopping streets, restaurants and cultural attractions are well known. Municipal sightseeing routes highlight Liberdade as a neighborhood where São Paulo's cultural diversity is particularly visible.

**The founding site, Viaduto do Chá and the Municipal Theatre** continue the historical story. Buildings and public spaces show how São Paulo evolved from a trading center into an enormous business city.

**The Municipal Market, Praça da República and Terraço Itália** add later chapters of urban development. The route also includes a station square and suburban railway station. These are listed sightseeing landmarks; they do not promise an individual ticket and a detailed interior visit at every stop.

The tour is described as lasting 6 hours. The standalone excursion listing, however, does not specify the guide's language, a list of paid admission tickets or transportation fares. Confirm these for your chosen booking rather than carrying over the terms of a different excursion.

## How the excursion connects to the Brazil motorcycle tour

The [10-day "Motorcycling through Brazil" itinerary](/brazil/tour/brazil-motorcycle-tour-10-days/) begins with arrival in São Paulo, transfer to a hotel and check-in. If time allows, an optional city sightseeing excursion can be added. The main motorcycle journey starts the following day, when the group collects the bikes and heads toward Capitólio through Minas Gerais state.

The route then continues via [Petrópolis](/brazil/place/petropolis/) to [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), follows the coast to [Paraty](/brazil/place/paraty/) and returns to São Paulo. The roads themselves matter as much as the cities, with changing mountain landscapes and coastal stops along the way.

The optional 6 hours at the start therefore need to be considered alongside arrival time, rest after the flight and preparation for the motorcycle stage. If the group arrives late, the city sightseeing excursion cannot be treated as a guaranteed visit.

## Why the sightseeing day and riding day are different

| Stage | Type of activity |
|---|---|
| [São Paulo sightseeing](/brazil/sao-paulo/sao-paulo-city-tour-6-hours/) | Optional city excursion |
| [10-day motorcycle tour](/brazil/tour/brazil-motorcycle-tour-10-days/) | Main motorcycle itinerary |

The city excursion introduces architecture and history. The motorcycle tour is built around covering a long route between regions. Although both may appear on the same page, their purposes and participation terms are different.

The motorcycle tour description specifies a group of at least 10 people, GS1250 motorcycles or similar, an 8-day rental with insurance, fuel, tolls, parking, a luggage support vehicle and guides on the main route. These conditions relate to the motorcycle product and **do not automatically establish** the transport type or price of the six-hour city excursion.

Travelers interested in this style of journey can visit the [motorcycle tours section](/interests/motorcycle-tours/); for São Paulo without motorbikes, see [local city excursions](/brazil/sao-paulo/).

## Exploring the city's history and modern life

The six-hour excursion focuses on the historic center and major city landmarks. If you are also interested in Avenida Paulista, Ibirapuera Park and graffiti districts, consider the [other São Paulo excursion](/brazil/sao-paulo/sao-paulo-historic-modern-graffiti/), where these places are explicitly part of the itinerary.

Municipal tourism routes also highlight Avenida Paulista, Liberdade and the historic triangle as distinct areas. This information can help you plan an independent free day, but does not make them automatically included stops on the six-hour tour discussed here.

São Paulo covers a vast area, and transfers between distant neighborhoods can take considerable time. Within a six-hour schedule, it is better to identify preferred highlights in advance than to expect detailed visits to every museum and park.

## What to confirm when booking

The main issue is the excursion's **optional status** relative to the motorcycle tour. Confirm your actual arrival time in São Paulo, whether the sightseeing outing can begin, its price, the guiding language, transportation and any admission tickets needed.

If the excursion follows an international flight, allow time for the airport transfer and hotel check-in. With a tight schedule, it is safer to rest before the motorcycle stage than to rush through stops or try to finish them after dark.

Compare other [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/) by travel style and main destinations. A city day at the start of a motorcycle tour and a São Paulo excursion included in a conventional group itinerary are different products.

## Frequently asked questions about the six-hour excursion as part of a tour

### Is the six-hour excursion included in the motorcycle tour price?

Inclusion is not confirmed. On the [ten-day motorcycle tour](/brazil/tour/brazil-motorcycle-tour-10-days/), it is described as an optional activity on the first day, subject to time and interest.

### When does the actual motorcycle route begin?

On day 2, after breakfast and collection of the motorcycles, the group departs São Paulo toward Capitólio. The first day is dedicated to arrival, hotel check-in and optional sightseeing.

### Are the cathedral and Liberdade on the excursion itinerary?

Yes. Both places are explicitly listed on the [six-hour São Paulo sightseeing route](/brazil/sao-paulo/sao-paulo-city-tour-6-hours/). Interior visits and any relevant tickets must be confirmed separately.

### How is it different from the half-day sightseeing excursion?

The [half-day excursion](/brazil/sao-paulo/sao-paulo-city-half-day-english/) is associated with a different group itinerary and explicitly includes an English-speaking guide and admission tickets. The six-hour excursion has its own list of historic landmarks and separate terms.

## Eight-hour São Paulo sightseeing tour: architecture and culture

[São Paulo](/brazil/place/sao-paulo/) is Brazil's largest metropolis, with museums and historic buildings alongside skyscrapers, markets, parks and neighborhoods shaped by different cultural traditions. To appreciate the architecture and daily life beyond the city's business image, it is worth setting aside a full day.

Ada Tours offers a [full-day city sightseeing excursion (8 hours)](/brazil/sao-paulo/sao-paulo-city-tour-8-hours/). It focuses on urban culture and landmarks, rather than a journey to the coast or a separate specialist museum program.

## How to explore the metropolis

São Paulo is enormous, so it is impossible to explore every district in depth in 8 hours. A successful tour requires selecting stops and allowing realistic transfer times. Some attractions are far apart, and traffic can substantially change the day's sequence.

Possible city landmarks to consider include the MASP museum, Ibirapuera Park, Liberdade and historic and modern architecture. Specific visits depend on the agreed itinerary, however. These examples should not be read as a guaranteed list of tickets and guided museum visits.

## Avenida Paulista and the MASP museum

Avenida Paulista is one of São Paulo's defining streets, lined with tall offices, cultural venues, restaurants and the **MASP** museum. The museum is known for its art collection and striking building, with an open space beneath the elevated volume.

If you particularly want to see MASP's exhibitions, allow extra time. Opening arrangements vary by weekday and exhibition, so a stop outside the building should not be confused with a full museum visit.

A walk along Paulista can reveal the contrast between modern buildings and preserved historic houses. Architectural eras often stand side by side in São Paulo.

## Historic center and Sé Cathedral

In the old city, the cathedral at Praça da Sé and buildings connected with São Paulo's rise as a major trading and industrial center are worth exploring. A walking stop allows you to appreciate façades and details of the streetscape that are easily missed from a car.

Time in the center should be planned around traffic and the precise drop-off point. An eight-hour sightseeing day needs a balance between stops and movement.

## Liberdade and the city's cultural life

Liberdade is associated with the history of Japanese immigration and the cultures of Brazil's Asian communities. Signs, shops, cafés and local traditions make this heritage visible in everyday neighborhood life. São Paulo was shaped by many waves of migration, and Liberdade is one of the clearest examples.

If your visit is focused on food, architecture or cultural history, arrange a stop in Liberdade in advance. A detour to the district cannot be guaranteed without an agreed itinerary.

## Ibirapuera Park

Ibirapuera contrasts with dense city buildings. Green spaces, paths, exhibition-pavilion architecture and museums provide a different experience. It is worth discussing as a possible sightseeing stop, especially if contemporary cultural institutions interest you.

Set your priorities before the day begins. Spending most of the time in the park or a museum will leave less time for other neighborhoods.

## Ada Tours duration and price

Our excursion lasts **8 hours** and costs **$183 per person**. Discounts may be available for groups of several people. The exact included services, guide language, museum tickets and itinerary are not specified as guaranteed terms and must be agreed separately. Do not assume admissions or meals are included simply because the tour lasts eight hours.

To compare this excursion with a longer trip around the country, see [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/). On the [12-day "São Paulo, Iguaçu, Rio, Ilha Grande and Paraty" itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-sao-paulo-iguazu-rio-ilha-grande-paraty-12-days/), São Paulo is one of the principal destinations. However, check the city-day plan in that tour rather than assuming all elements of the separate eight-hour excursion are included.

## What to bring and how to prioritize

Comfortable shoes for short walks, drinking water and light clothing suitable for the weather are useful on a city tour. Check opening hours in advance for museums and historic buildings. Choose your priorities according to your interests: history, modern architecture, art or cultural neighborhoods.

## Frequently asked questions

### How long is the São Paulo excursion?

The excursion is planned for **8 hours**.

### Can you visit both MASP and Ibirapuera?

You can discuss both stops, but visiting exhibitions in depth and walking in the park take time. The final sequence is agreed separately.

### How much does the sightseeing tour cost?

The price is **$183 per person**; discounts may be available for several participants.

### Are museum tickets included?

Inclusion of those tickets has not been separately confirmed. Check admission prices and conditions for the specific museums when booking.

## São Paulo: historic center, Ibirapuera and graffiti on one excursion

The [São Paulo sightseeing excursion](/brazil/sao-paulo/sao-paulo-historic-modern-graffiti/) combines several very different urban environments. It begins in the historic center, continues through the modern city and Ibirapuera Park, and ends in a graffiti district. This sequence helps explain why [São Paulo](/brazil/place/sao-paulo/) is known as a huge business metropolis yet retains vibrant cultural neighborhoods, historic monuments and public spaces.

We run the excursion through the named districts and attractions **with a guide**. The exact duration and guiding language are agreed on booking, so do not assume the route is a standard three-, four- or six-hour walk.

## Historic center: where the city began

The first part of the excursion visits Praça da Sé and the cathedral, where the city's religious and civic history is particularly evident. The route then includes São Paulo's founding site, Viaduto do Chá, the Municipal Theatre, Praça da República and other significant places in the center.

Buildings from different periods stand side by side: monumental squares, theater façades, shopping streets and high-rise structures. For visitors, this is an excellent way to understand how São Paulo developed from a small settlement into Brazil's largest city. Instead of a single isolated monument, you see streets whose architecture and uses have changed over time.

The route also passes the square near the railway station, the Municipal Market and the Terraço Itália building. Mentioning the market does not mean a food tasting is included, and seeing the theater exterior does not guarantee entry to the auditorium. Confirm any interior visits separately.

## Liberdade's Japanese district: a different São Paulo

The Japanese neighborhood of Liberdade stands out for its streetscape, shops, restaurants and the cultural history of immigrants. It illustrates the diversity of São Paulo's population. Alongside the business center, communities developed whose distinctive traditions remain visible in the city's everyday life.

On our itinerary, Liberdade is a separate stop in the historical section. If food or shopping is of special interest, arrange time for it: neither should automatically be treated as a complete standalone excursion within this city overview.

## Avenida Paulista and Ibirapuera Park: the modern city

After the historic center, travelers explore Avenida Paulista, one of the city's main avenues. Contemporary architecture, business life and cultural institutions offer a different perspective on São Paulo.

The next contrast is [Ibirapuera Park](/brazil/place/sao-paulo/), a green area with walking paths, water features and places to stroll. Here you will see the obelisk commemorating events of 1932 and the Monument to the Bandeiras, dedicated to historical expeditions into Brazil's interior.

The park belongs to the wider history of the city, rather than representing a promise of an extended nature break. The time available for walking depends on the agreed excursion timetable.

## Graffiti district: contemporary street art

The final part of the itinerary focuses on modern districts and a graffiti neighborhood. São Paulo's murals show creativity beyond museum galleries: paintings change, new works appear on some walls and the city itself becomes an exhibition space.

No confirmed list of artists or individual murals is attached to this particular excursion. It is better to think of this part as an introduction to street-art culture than to promise a particular painting or the continued existence of a specific mural.

For more on this theme, browse [cultural and historical journeys](/interests/culture-and-history/) in Brazil. Architecture, migration history and contemporary art come together especially clearly along this city route.

## Preparing for a varied city itinerary

Several distant neighborhoods are combined in one excursion. First agree the exact duration, meeting point, order of transfers and walking segments. São Paulo has heavy traffic, and actual journey times can substantially affect how long you spend at each stop.

Comfortable shoes and a small supply of drinking water are more useful than heavy luggage. If you wish to add a museum, a dedicated food stop or shopping time, discuss the changes in advance: the standard selection is designed to introduce different parts of the city.

| Itinerary section | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Praça da Sé and the center | City history |
| Liberdade | Cultural communities |
| Paulista and Ibirapuera | The modern metropolis |
| Graffiti district | Street art |

When comparing [São Paulo excursions](/brazil/sao-paulo/), decide whether you want a broad overview or a closer look at one subject. A day with many stops gives you a sense of the city's geography, but it does not replace a dedicated museum or culinary experience.

## Frequently asked questions about the São Paulo excursion

### Which places does the excursion cover?

The historic center, Praça da Sé, the Japanese district, Avenida Paulista, Ibirapuera Park and the graffiti district, as well as the historic squares and buildings listed in the itinerary.

### How many hours does it last?

We agree the exact duration when booking. The number of stops alone does not determine the time required.

### Are museum and theater tickets included?

The guided route introduces city attractions, but museum admissions have not been confirmed as included. Interior visits and extra costs must be clarified when arranging the program.

### Can I spend more time exploring street art?

That would require changing the itinerary and the time available. On our general sightseeing route, the graffiti district is the final section; a separate extended art tour is not included.
